symptomShortText: Induction case depth below minimum on shafts hardened on COIL1 - inductor coupling gap too wide

defect.defectText: Insufficient case depth after induction hardening

causesIshikawa.description: Operator loaded shafts per work instruction, no deviation
WC-HEAT-03-COIL1 locating bushing worn 1.2mm - inductor coupling gap 3.4mm vs 1.8-2.2mm, less energy into the surface
Hardening recipe HT-S150-02 power and scan speed unchanged
42CrMo4 bar lot BS-3402 chemistry within specification
Microhardness tester MH-02 verified on reference block

fiveWhyChain.question: Why was the case depth below minimum?
fiveWhyChain.answer: Effective case depth measured 1.32mm against 1.80-2.40mm on shafts hardened on COIL1

fiveWhyChain.question: Why did COIL1 transfer less energy into the shaft?
fiveWhyChain.answer: The inductor coupling gap was 3.4mm instead of 1.8-2.2mm, so the heated layer stayed shallow

fiveWhyChain.question: Why was the coupling gap too wide? (root cause)
fiveWhyChain.answer: The locating bushing had worn 1.2mm and the gap was not checked at setup

actions.actionText: Quarantine 40 drive shafts from batch B-70395 and perform 100% eddy current case depth sort
Replace worn inductor locating bushing on WC-HEAT-03-COIL1 and re-qualify the coupling gap
Add coupling gap check to the induction setup checklist across all heat treat lines

fmeaLink.description: Shallow hardening depth from inductor coupling gap drift

lessonsLearned.whatWorked: Splitting results by coil station pointed straight at COIL1 hardware
lessonsLearned.whatDidnt: Coupling gap was set once at installation and never re-checked

isIsNot.isWhereWhenItHappens: S150 bearing journal - WC-HEAT-03-COIL1 - batch B-70395, July 2026
isIsNot.isNotWhereWhenItDoesnt: WC-HEAT-03-COIL2 - same bar lot BS-3402 and same recipe
isIsNot.notes: Defect follows the coil station, not the material or recipe
